entities.text: Rubeena Begum And Ors vs Ashok Kumar And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The captioned appeal is by the claimants questioning the quantum determined by the Tribunal in MVC No.265/2016.
Respondent No.2/insurance company admits its liability.

The appeal is therefore purely on quantum.
2.
The claimants filed a claim petition for having lost one Md. Abdul Khadeer in a road traffic accident dated 10.05.2015.

The appellants contended that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/-
and hence filed a claim petition.
3. The Tribunal for having answered issue No.1 in the affirmative, held that the cause of accident is on account of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending goods Mahindra vehicle.

While determining the compensation, the Tribunal notionally assessed the income NC:
2024:KHC-K:9545 of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month in absence of income proof and by adding 40% of the income towards future prospects, awarded Rs.11,34,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
The Tribunal in all awarded Rs.12,24,000/-.
4. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/insurance company.
This Court has independently assessed the judgment under challenge.
5. Though the claimants have asserted that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, there is absolutely no evidence to substantiate the notional income of the deceased.
Though the Tribunal was justified in notionally assessing the income, however, the income notionally assessed at Rs.6,000/- is on the lower side.
In absence of income proof, this Court is inclined to place reliance on the income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident is of the year NC: 2024:KHC-K:9545 2015.
Accordingly, the income is notionally assessed at Rs.8,000/- and by adding 40% of the income towards future prospects, the income is taken at Rs.11,200/-.
There are five dependents.
Hence, 1/4th is deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
After deducting 1/4th, the income is assessed at Rs.8,400/- and by applying a multiplier of 18, the compensation payable under the head of loss of dependency works out to Rs.18,14,400/-.
6. Under conventional heads, the claimants are entitled for Rs.2,30,000/- as there are five dependents.

The accident is of the year 2015 and applying the principles laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi1, 10% escalation is awarded for every three years on conventional heads which works out to Rs.46,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The total compensation re-determined by this Court works out (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC-K:9545 to Rs.20,90,400/-
as against Rs.12,24,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

7. In the light of findings recorded supra, this Court passes the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.8,66,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the Rubeena Begum And Ors vs Ashok Kumar And Anr on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139638197/
3 date of petition till its realization.
